title: Don't Download Twice
story:
**From:** Amara Okafor
**Subject:** climate-fetch rebuilds are eating the satellite budget

Every time I touch one line of `requirements.txt`, pip downloads every package again. The Dockerfile even has `--no-cache-dir` in it, because someone once told me that keeps images small. Ten rebuilds a day over a metered link adds up fast.

Can you make the build keep pip's download cache between builds, without baking the cache into the image? Build the result as `kestrel/climate-fetch:1.0`.
objectives: Edit `/workspace/Dockerfile` so the pip install step uses a BuildKit cache mount on `/root/.cache/pip`
Build the image as `kestrel/climate-fetch:1.0`; it must still run and print `climate-fetch ready`
startingState: `/workspace` holds a working Dockerfile, `requirements.txt` and `fetch.py` for the climate-fetch tool, but nothing has been built yet.
hints: The build engine (BuildKit) can mount a directory that persists between builds but never becomes part of an image layer. That is exactly what a package manager's download cache needs.
Attach it to the install step with `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=DIR ...`. pip's cache lives in `/root/.cache/pip`, and `--no-cache-dir` would tell pip to ignore it, so it has to go.

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
    pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY fetch.py .
CMD ["python", "fetch.py"]
```
Then `docker build -t kestrel/climate-fetch:1.0 .`

files.content:
FROM python:3.12-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY fetch.py .
CMD ["python", "fetch.py"]

validation.description: The Dockerfile installs with `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip` and without `--no-cache-dir`

solution:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.12-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
    pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY fetch.py .
CMD ["python", "fetch.py"]
EOF
debrief: The second build skipped the download because the cache mount survived between builds, and it never became part of a layer, so the image stays lean. Pro tip: the same trick works for `apk` (`/var/cache/apk`), Go (`/root/.cache/go-build`) and `npm`.
